items.title: Digital Asset Standards Consultation – Closes 27 Nov 2026
items.desc: ASIC consultation on guidance and standards for the new Digital Asset Platform (DAP) and Tokenised Custody Platform (TCP) AFSL regime closes 27 November 2026. Final instruments expected March 2027; licence applications open 8 April 2027.

items.title: FFSP Relief Extension Consultation – Closes 4 Dec 2026
items.desc: ASIC proposes extending the existing sufficient equivalence and limited connection relief for foreign financial services providers from 31 March 2027 to 30 September 2027. Submissions close 4 December 2026. Final position expected early 2027.

items.title: FAR Simplification – Changes Due to Commence Early 2027
items.desc: APRA and ASIC are finalising Financial Accountability Regime changes: dropping prescribed key functions from the register, raising change notification thresholds, and reducing accountability map update requirements by at least half. Commencement planned early 2027.

items.title: Digital Asset AFSL – Enforcement Now Active
items.desc: ASIC's no-action position for digital asset businesses expired 30 September 2026. Firms operating without an AFSL, variation, or authorised representative arrangement are now exposed to civil and criminal penalties. ASIC is actively enforcing.

items.title: Digital Assets Framework – AFSL Applications Open 8 Apr 2027
items.desc: Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 commences 8 April 2027. DAP and TCP operators can lodge AFSL applications from that date. Full compliance required by October 2027. ASIC roadmap guidance to be released March 2027.

items.title: AML/CTF Amendment Bill 2026 – Before Parliament
items.desc: The AML/CTF Amendment Bill 2026 is currently before Parliament. Proposes expanded AUSTRAC CEO powers to restrict high-risk products and delivery channels (including crypto ATMs). Monitor for passage and assess operational impact.

items.title: Independent AML/CTF Review – Due by 31 Mar 2027
items.desc: Higher-risk reporting entities must complete an independent review of their AML/CTF program within 12 months of the 31 March 2026 reform commencement. Deadline is 31 March 2027. Engage reviewers and confirm scope now to avoid a crunch.

items.title: AUSTRAC Enforcement – Infringement Notices Issued
items.desc: AUSTRAC has begun issuing infringement notices and section 167 notices to businesses providing designated services without enrolling. Tranche 2 entities not yet enrolled should treat this as urgent — enrolment is overdue.

items.title: Tranche 2 Obligations Fully In Force
items.desc: Lawyers, accountants, real estate professionals, conveyancers, jewellers and trust & company service providers have been subject to AML/CTF obligations since 1 July 2026. All must have an AML/CTF program, compliance officer and trained staff.

items.title: Annual Compliance Report – New FY Cycle, Due 30 Sep 2027
items.desc: No compliance report required for the Jan–Jun 2026 transition period. First report under the new financial-year cycle covers 1 Jul 2026–30 Jun 2027, due 30 September 2027. Build data collection processes now.

items.title: Rate of Return Instrument – Final Decision Due Dec 2026
items.desc: AER is targeting December 2026 for the final 2026 RORI and explanatory statement. Submissions on the post-draft equity beta and market risk premium discussion paper closed 23 October 2026. Final instrument sets allowed returns for the next regulatory cycle.

items.title: AER 2026–27 Compliance & Enforcement Priorities Active
items.desc: AER's 2026–27 priorities focus on vulnerable consumer outcomes, smart meter rollout, power system security, network safety and competition, and Part 10 National Gas Rules reporting compliance.

items.title: Minimum Disconnection Amount Now $500 – Confirm Procedures
items.desc: AER raised the minimum amount before a retailer may disconnect a customer under NECF from $300 to $500, effective 1 July 2026. Confirm disconnection systems, scripts and procedures have been updated.

items.title: Exemptions Guidelines 2026 Review – Consultation Ongoing
items.desc: AER's review of the Exemptions Guidelines is ongoing, proposing reduced regulatory burden for commercial embedded network retrofits to align with flexible trading reforms. Monitor for final decision timing.
